decision_basis: Release readiness accepts opaque fixture bytes and digest-shaped evaluator and provider references without verifying their semantic schema or referenced artifact bytes.
Synthetic provenance-free evaluator rows can produce a claim-eligible verified-net-win receipt without an authenticated evaluator release or claim authorization.
Retry usage is charged to journal budgets but only the terminal attempt reaches decision statistics, which can understate treatment cost and tokens.
A crash-torn final journal append is rejected forever, so the frozen interruption-recovery protocol cannot recover its own schedule.
These are outcome-determining evidence, measurement, and recovery rule changes, so the frozen amendment policy requires a new protocol id.
next_protocol_requirements: schema-validated public fixtures and content-addressed workspace snapshots
byte-verified provider, runner, transcript, evaluator, and check-evidence artifacts
a preregistered evaluator identity with standard authenticated release and result receipts
real-versus-synthetic evidence labeling with synthetic rows permanently claim-ineligible
cumulative retry usage in both budgets and decision statistics
locked recovery of only an unterminated final fragment with a content-addressed recovery receipt
ambiguous provider-dispatch reconciliation without automatic reinvocation
